title: Validation of neuromusculoskeletal simulations of aged spines
summary:
This study investigates how spinal load distribution changes in individuals over 50 years of age. Participants who undergo a specialized spinal X-ray examination as part of their clinical care will additionally perform everyday movements such as bending, twisting, and walking. These movements, together with muscle activity, will be measured in a gait laboratory.
Based on the imaging and motion data, individualized computational models of the spine will be created to calculate the acting forces within the spine. The aim of the study is to improve the understanding of age-related changes of the spine and thereby contribute to improved diagnostics and treatment strategies in the long term.

interventions.name: EOSedge@ images of the thoracolumbar spine of patients are processed to 3D geometrical models, soft tissue elements are included and material parameters adjusted to age, sex and weight to develop patient-specific musculoskeletal in silico models, forward-dynamic simulation of active spine movement s

Movement analysis is for same patients as in Arm 1,  kinematics will be captured using an optical 3D motion capture system and reflective markers, muscle activity will be recorded via electromyography, comparison with predicted personalized results from simulations

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- EOSedge® imaging of the spine (at least the complete thoracolumbar region) in the orthopedic outpatient clinic based on a medical indication and with sufficient EOS image quality
- Ability to independently perform simple trunk movements (flexion, extension, lateral bending, axial rotation) and walking on a treadmill
- Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Previous spinal surgeries (e.g., fusion, implants, disc prostheses, injections)
- Diseases or functional limitations that significantly impair motion analysis, such as severe central neurological or musculoskeletal disorders
- Pronounced scoliosis (> 20° Cobb angle)
- Obesity (BMI > 30 kg/m²)
- Active implants or devices that could interfere with electromagnetic measurements
- Pregnancy
- Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
